Staryy Ostropil Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Staryy Ostropil was the birthplace in 1757 of Hershele Ostropoler, a beloved trickster and jester figure in Yiddish folklore, associated with the court of Tzaddik Boruch of Medzhybizh, a grandson of the Baal Shem Tov. The town's wooden synagogue, built in the 17th century, survived until the early 20th. This cemetery holds the revived borders of a mass grave from the Khmelnytsky Uprising of 1648, suggesting the cemetery already existed at that time; it was fenced by the Ohalei Tzadikim — Gader Avot union, documented at several other sites in this collection, in 2014. In late June 1942, 581 Jews of Staryy Ostropil were executed in Starokostyantyniv together with Jews from other districts, and the 73 remaining were expelled to Lubar in Zhytomyr district, documented elsewhere in this collection, where they were murdered.
